title: RID_Alloc: the id that gets validator 0x7FFFFFFF matches every free slot of every other owner, so free_rid() crashes after 2^31 RIDs (4.5+, regression from #105538)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible: 4.7.stable.official (5b4e0cb0f), macOS 15.7.9, Apple M2 (Metal, Mobile renderer) and --headless.
By source: core/templates/rid_owner.h is the same in 4.7.1-stable, 4.7.2-stable and master (d824ca9fe2, 2026-10-14);
the lines came in with c6c06a966a ("Allow chunk validator to wrap around in RID_Alloc so that we do not need to crash
once we have made 2^31 allocations", PR #105538, first released in 4.5-stable).

### System information

macOS 15.7.9 (24G830), Mac14,15 (M2, 8 GB). Godot 4.7.stable.official (5b4e0cb0f) from Homebrew.

### Issue description

_allocate_rid() takes `validator = 1 + (_gen_id() % 0x7FFFFFFF)`, so validators run 1..0x7FFFFFFF and the id
k * 0x7FFFFFFF - 1 gets 0x7FFFFFFF. A free slot holds 0xFFFFFFFF, and owns() compares
`(slot.validator & 0x7FFFFFFF) == validator`, so for that one RID every owner whose chunk covers its slot index and
holds that slot free answers owns() == true. Before #105538 owns() refused 0x7FFFFFFF explicitly and _allocate_rid
crashed on purpose instead. Every dispatcher that tries owners in turn (RenderingDevice::_free_internal,
RenderingServerDefault::_free, the physics servers' free_rid, ...) then takes the wrong owner's branch: get_or_null()
returns nullptr (or, where the compiler folds the null path, prints "Attempting to use an uninitialized RID" and traps)
and the branch dereferences it.

The counter is process-wide, so a 2D app that redraws a lot reaches it in hours. Our app redraws one large CanvasItem
every frame (draw_circle / draw_colored_polygon / draw_polyline / draw_arc, each a polygon of up to four RD RIDs made
and freed per frame; several hundred polygons a frame, by the run lengths below). It crashed 13 times on macOS after 2.9 to 8.5 hours, always in
CanvasItem::_redraw_callback -> RenderingServer canvas_item_clear -> RendererCanvasRenderRD::free_polygon ->
RenderingDevice::free_rid -> _free_internal, in the texture (1), framebuffer (4), sampler (7, with "Attempting to use an
uninitialized RID at: get_or_null (./core/templates/rid_owner.h:247)" then SIGTRAP) or vertex-buffer (1) branch, for
each of the polygon's four RIDs in turn (reports attached). The run lengths match 2^31 RIDs at 70k-205k RIDs a second.

A second, rarer effect of the same wrap: once validators restart at 1, a new RID can share its validator with a
long-lived RID made early in the process; when both sit at the same slot index in two owners, a dispatcher that checks
the long-lived one's owner first frees the wrong resource.

### Steps to reproduce

(about 40 s; no project needed beyond an empty project.godot)
    extends SceneTree
    func _init() -> void:
        var shape: RID = PhysicsServer2D.circle_shape_create()   # gives the shape owner a chunk...
        PhysicsServer2D.free_rid(shape)                           # ...whose slots are now all free
        while rid_allocate_id() < 0x7FFFFFFD:                     # the counter to just before the id
            pass
        var body: RID = PhysicsServer2D.body_create()             # validator 0x7FFFFFFF
        print("validator 0x%X" % (body.get_id() >> 32))
        PhysicsServer2D.free_rid(body)                            # shape_owner.owns(body) is true: crash
        quit()
    godot --headless --path . --script res://repro.gd
Output on 4.7.0: "validator 0x7FFFFFFF", then "ERROR: Attempting to use an uninitialized RID at: get_or_null
(./core/templates/rid_owner.h:247)" and "Program crashed with signal 5" (log attached). With one more
rid_allocate_id() before body_create() (the id spent by nobody) the body gets validator 0x1 and frees cleanly.

SUGGESTED FIX
    uint32_t validator = 1 + (uint32_t)(_gen_id() % 0x7FFFFFFE);   // 1..0x7FFFFFFE: never the free marker's low bits
and, as before #105538, `(validator != 0x7FFFFFFF) &&` in owns(). That closes the crash; the post-wrap collision
needs the dispatchers not to rely on owns() alone across owners (or a wider validator).

WORKAROUND WE SHIP
Once a frame, on the main thread, the app reads the counter with rid_allocate_id() and, when the id that would carry
0x7FFFFFFF is near, calls rid_allocate_id() until it has passed it (and the first validators of the new round).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
